formats.name: gwf
notes: Backend aliases resolve through gwpy GWF readers.
Public direct I/O includes TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads.
TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads accept ordered list/tuple sources of .gwf paths.
Multi-file GWF reads merge in time-span order; contiguous spans join normally.
Gaps raise by default and with gap='raise'; pad=<value> or gap='pad' fills gaps, and gap='ignore' concatenates without filling.
When start/end extend beyond available data, the default gap='raise' behavior rejects the request; pass pad=<value> or gap='pad' to fill the outer interval.
For multi-file GWF reads without an explicit channel selector, channel auto-discovery uses the first source and assumes the remaining sources contain compatible channel names.
gap='ignore' does not pad missing samples inside gaps or outside a requested start/end interval.
Overlapping spans are rejected by default and with gap='raise'; gap='ignore' concatenates files in span order and permits overlap concatenation.
TimeSeriesMatrix reader remains an implementation convenience path until it is published explicitly in the user guide.

formats.name: hdf.ndscope
metadata_requirements: NDScope writers preserve canonical rate_hz and gps_start metadata; readers also accept sample_rate as a compatibility alias for rate_hz.
notes: Public direct I/O is collection-first and TimeSeriesDict-only.
Single-series and matrix registry adapters are implementation convenience paths, not public contract surface.

formats.name: hdf5
metadata_requirements: Collection HDF5 files must preserve manifest key maps and entry order for published dict/list families.
Published readers and writers must round-trip core axis metadata and units needed for reconstruction.
notes: Published usage should set format="hdf5" explicitly because .h5/.hdf5 overlaps specialized HDF5 families and auto-identification is not uniform across classes.
Public HDF5 direct I/O covers documented time-series, frequency-series, spectrogram, histogram, and event-table families.
GWpy segment classes remain part of the broader registry-backed implementation surface, but they are not part of the published HDF5 direct-I/O contract in this slice.
FrequencySeriesMatrix and SpectrogramMatrix remain outside the published HDF5 contract until matrix-axis serialization is hardened.
Field classes remain intentionally outside this schema slice pending a dedicated direct-I/O audit.

formats.name: xml.diaggui
notes: Public direct I/O is TimeSeriesDict-first because DiagGUI XML is product-driven.
TimeSeries and TimeSeriesMatrix readers remain registry adapters, but public guidance requires explicit format="xml.diaggui" and products=...
FrequencySeries and FrequencySeriesDict DTTXML direct shims, and FrequencySeriesDict / FrequencySeriesMatrix registry adapters, are implementation-only and not part of the public direct-I/O contract.

formats.name: csv
metadata_requirements: Manifest-backed collection directories must preserve original entry keys and per-entry unit metadata.
notes: Published CSV direct I/O is limited to TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict.
Single-file CSV is a lightweight exchange path; do not rely on it for complete name, channel, or unit metadata preservation across GWpy-compatible readers.
TimeSeriesDict supports both single-file CSV reads and manifest-backed collection-directory reads and writes.

Numeric and configured component-column timestamps must have regular source cadence before any requested resampling; UTC components are compared as continuous GPS instants, and malformed source rows raise ValueError with physical line numbers.
A finite positive sample_rate declares source cadence and is honoured for single-row input; without it, the legacy one-second fallback remains.
resample must be a finite positive target rate; output values are evaluated on the exact target-cadence grid for requested channels without relabelling source samples.

Absolute float64 time-axis rounding error and spacing must each be strictly below half the cadence; resampling is limited to 10000000 requested-channel output values across the complete top-level single- or multi-file read before allocation.
Numeric timestamps retain the legacy GPS-second interpretation; time_scale and time_unit are not part of the v0.1.14 contract.
Broader registry adapters such as TimeSeriesMatrix, FrequencySeries, Spectrogram, and EventTable remain implementation surface only.

formats.name: txt
metadata_requirements: Manifest-backed collection directories must preserve original entry keys and per-entry unit metadata.
notes: Published TXT direct I/O is limited to TimeSeries files and TimeSeriesDict collection directories.
Single-series TXT reads and writes require explicit format="txt".
Multi-channel TXT direct I/O uses manifest-backed collection directories rather than single text files.

formats.name: pickle
notes: Pickle compatibility is currently provided through pickle.dumps()/pickle.loads() and shelve, not through published direct .read()/.write() methods.
Security guidance remains important, but Pickle is intentionally outside the public direct-I/O contract.

formats.name: root
notes: Published ROOT direct I/O is intentionally limited to EventTable.
EventTable .root files are auto-identified by the live registry; read/write require the optional uproot backend.
Collection .write(..., format="root") helpers remain PyROOT-based interop conveniences and are not part of the published direct-I/O contract.

formats.name: sdb
metadata_requirements: Published SDB reads must preserve weather/archive column names and derived physical units after conversion.
When present, every usUnits value must be the integer 1; when absent, the legacy US customary unit assumption is used.
dateTime values must be integer Unix seconds with regular cadence in database storage order.
notes: Published SDB direct I/O is read-only for TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict.
Only the sdb format token and .sdb auto-identification are public.
Duplicate, backward, missing, or overlarge dateTime gaps raise ValueError before a time axis is constructed.
Rowid tables use SQLite rowid/B-tree order, which is not insertion chronology; WITHOUT ROWID tables use declared primary-key order including direction and collation.
TimeSeriesMatrix read support remains an implementation convenience path, not a published contract entry.

formats.name: wav
metadata_requirements: Published WAV direct I/O must preserve sample-rate timing and treat t0=0.0 as a convenience default rather than an absolute timestamp claim.
notes: Published WAV direct I/O covers TimeSeries read/write and TimeSeriesDict read.
TimeSeriesMatrix read support remains an implementation convenience path until it is published explicitly.
WAV write is intentionally single-series only in the current public contract.

formats.name: flac
metadata_requirements: Published compressed-audio direct I/O must preserve sample-rate timing and treat t0=0.0 as a convenience default rather than an absolute timestamp claim.
notes: Published FLAC direct I/O covers TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads and writes.
The implementation depends on pydub; some environments also need ffmpeg/libav.
TimeSeriesMatrix adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: ogg
metadata_requirements: Published compressed-audio direct I/O must preserve sample-rate timing and treat t0=0.0 as a convenience default rather than an absolute timestamp claim.
notes: Published OGG direct I/O covers TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads and writes.
The implementation depends on pydub; some environments also need ffmpeg/libav.
TimeSeriesMatrix adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: mp3
metadata_requirements: Published compressed-audio direct I/O must preserve sample-rate timing and treat t0=0.0 as a convenience default rather than an absolute timestamp claim.
notes: Published MP3 direct I/O covers TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads and writes.
The implementation depends on pydub and typically also requires ffmpeg/libav.
TimeSeriesMatrix adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: m4a
metadata_requirements: Published compressed-audio direct I/O must preserve sample-rate timing and treat t0=0.0 as a convenience default rather than an absolute timestamp claim.
notes: Published M4A direct I/O covers TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads and writes.
The implementation depends on pydub and typically also requires ffmpeg/libav.
TimeSeriesMatrix adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: gbd
metadata_requirements: Published GBD reads must preserve timezone-resolved epoch handling and keep configured digital channels binarized as dimensionless data.
notes: Published GBD direct I/O is read-only for the TimeSeries family.
Public reads require timezone=... because the source stores local wall-clock timestamps.
GUI auto-load is not part of the published GBD contract because it cannot supply timezone implicitly.

formats.name: tdms
metadata_requirements: Published TDMS reads must preserve group/channel naming and waveform timing from wf_increment or TDMS timestamp properties.
notes: Published TDMS direct I/O is read-only for the TimeSeries family.
The implementation depends on nptdms and should raise ImportError with installation guidance when that dependency is unavailable.

formats.name: mseed
metadata_requirements: Published MiniSEED reads must preserve gap handling semantics, with NaN padding as the default merge behavior unless gap='raise' is requested.
notes: Published MiniSEED direct I/O is collection-first through TimeSeriesDict.
The legacy alias 'miniseed' must remain equivalent to canonical 'mseed'.
Single-series and matrix registry adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: sac
metadata_requirements: Published SAC direct I/O must preserve ObsPy-backed timing metadata needed to reconstruct the waveform as a TimeSeriesDict.
notes: Published SAC direct I/O is collection-first through TimeSeriesDict.
Single-series and matrix registry adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: gse2
metadata_requirements: Published GSE2 direct I/O must preserve ObsPy-backed timing metadata needed to reconstruct the waveform as a TimeSeriesDict.
notes: Published GSE2 direct I/O is collection-first through TimeSeriesDict.
Single-series and matrix registry adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: knet
metadata_requirements: Published K-NET reads must preserve channel identity and ObsPy-derived timing metadata through the TimeSeriesDict interface.
notes: Published K-NET direct I/O is read-only and collection-first through TimeSeriesDict.
Single-series and matrix registry adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: win
metadata_requirements: Published WIN reads must preserve patched delta decoding and the resulting channel/sample-rate metadata through the TimeSeriesDict interface.
Global WIN packet timestamps must advance by exactly one second; duplicate timestamps, backward timestamps, and global gaps must raise ValueError.

A channel may start after the first packet or end before the last packet, and its first appearance defines its channel-local t0; after a channel starts, reappearance following an internal packet gap must raise ValueError.
A duplicate channel block within one packet or a sample-rate change for an existing channel must raise ValueError.
Packet and channel payload lengths and decoded sample counts must be bounded and validated so malformed, truncated, or overlong payloads raise ValueError without an oversized read.
Cumulative delta decoding must not wrap at int32 bounds, and only a BCD year transition from 99 to 00 advances the supplied century.
notes: Published WIN direct I/O is read-only and collection-first through TimeSeriesDict.
The alias 'win32' must remain equivalent to canonical 'win' at the public-contract level.
WIN header time is interpreted as UTC and reported with one warning per top-level read, including multi-file reads.
Single-series and matrix registry adapters remain implementation conveniences.

formats.name: ats
metadata_requirements: Published ATS reads must preserve header-derived sample rate, epoch handling, and on-disk scaling through the public single-series and dict entrypoints.
notes: Published ATS direct I/O covers TimeSeries and TimeSeriesDict reads.
TimeSeriesMatrix read support remains an implementation convenience path.

formats.name: ats.mth5
metadata_requirements: Published ATS.MTH5 reads must remain a narrow single-series path and preserve MTH5-derived timing metadata when the dependency is available.
Channel data must be one-dimensional and non-empty, with a finite positive sample rate and a valid start time.
Components Ex and Ey require mV/km; Hx, Hy, and Hz require nT. Raw channel values are not rescaled.
notes: Published ATS.MTH5 direct I/O is intentionally limited to TimeSeries.read(..., format='ats.mth5').
TimeSeriesDict.read(..., format='ats.mth5') is rejected before optional dependency lookup.
Source timing and units are authoritative; epoch, timezone, unit, and other reader overrides are rejected rather than ignored.
The implementation uses mth5.read_file(..., file_type='metronix') from mth5>=0.6.8 and raises ImportError with installation guidance when that dependency is unavailable.

formats.name: nc
notes: Public direct I/O covers the TimeSeries family only.
The legacy alias 'netcdf4' must remain equivalent to the canonical 'nc' format token.
The public auto-identified extension is .nc; .netcdf4 is a format-token alias, not a documented extension alias.

formats.name: zarr
metadata_requirements: Each array must store sample_rate or dt timing metadata unless the reader is given an explicit recovery override.
notes: Public direct I/O covers the TimeSeries family only.
Legacy stores without timing metadata are recoverable only through explicit sample_rate_override or dt_override.
